subject: Request: temporary night support window carveout - proposed P2 amendment
messages:
From: Danielle Park <dpark@finnovate.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Night maintenance overlap — ask for temporary P2 response window

Hi Michael / Ben,

Quick note from the operations side at Finnovate — we have a recurring end-of-month backup/maintenance window that touches a small subset of our payment processing batch jobs between 00:30–02:30 PT. During that window our on-call platform briefly loses some SNMP metrics and we get a flurry of low-priority alerts that our SREs classify as P2.

Because those alerts are noise during the backup window, we want to request a short-term amendment to our support commitments so P2 responses overnight (00:00–06:00 PT) are extended to a 4-hour initial response for a 3-week period, while P1 remains unchanged. Proposed effective window: 2025-09-12 through 2025-10-02.

We believe this is the least-disruptive option for both teams and will reduce paging fatigue. As context, we plan to:
- Limit the carveout to the small batch domain (payment-batch cluster), not platform-wide.
- Provide a daily status channel in our joint Slack channel during the first week.

Attached: finnovate_maintenance_schedule.pdf (shows the nightly snapshots). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept that temporary change and what compensating controls you need?

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can coordinate our runbook owners.

Best,
Danielle Park
Head of SRE, Finnovate
ops@finnovate.com

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Night maintenance overlap — ask for temporary P2 response window

Ben — forwarding an ask from a mid-market customer (Finnovate). See attached schedule.

Summary of their ask: temporary adjustment to overnight P2 response window (00:00–06:00 PT) to 4 hours for ~3 weeks, P1 unchanged. They want to limit scope to the payment-batch cluster.

Can you:
1) Propose a concrete mitigation plan (how we keep P1 guarantees and triage P2 noise).
2) Draft a short amendment (one paragraph) we can present to the customer and push through legal/CS.
3) Confirm operational impact on our on-call rotation and any cost/credit implications.

I want a recommendation by EOD tomorrow so I can reply to Danielle with a firm yes/no and the terms. CCing Laura for visibility — if this needs leadership sign-off, flag it.

Thanks,
Michael
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Sep 8, 2025 at 3:12 PM Danielle Park <dpark@finnovate.com> wrote:
> Hi Michael / Ben,
>
> Quick note from the operations side at Finnovate — we have a recurring end-of-month backup/maintenance window...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 01:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Night maintenance overlap — ask for temporary P2 response window

Thanks for the ping, Michael — sketched a plan below after chatting with infra.

Plan (operational + compensations):
- Scope: payment-batch cluster only (tagged payment-batch/*). All other services unaffected.
- Effective dates: 2025-09-12 00:00 PT — 2025-10-02 23:59 PT.
- P1: unchanged (1 hour response SLA) — always paged to on-call.
- P2 (00:00–06:00 PT): initial response target extended to 4 hours; triage via automated filters so only actionable P2s escalate to humans.
- Escalation path:
  * Primary on-call (platform): handle P1. If primary confirms it's payment-batch noise, they acknowledge and attach "noise" tag.
  * Secondary on-call (payments owner): if incident elevates to functional degradation (e.g., batch failures impacting settlement), promote to P1 and escalate to engineering lead.
- Compensating controls: instrumentation to catch actual failures (end-to-end job failures trigger immediate P1). Nightly health-check and automated reroute to Dedicated fallback pool if payments cluster latency > 800ms for 10 consecutive minutes.
- Runbook changes: brief append to existing payment-batch runbook + a short nightly checklist.

I've attached a short draft amendment and a runbook diff: proposed_sla_amendment_draft.docx, runbook_night_handoff.md.

Operational impact: we'll add one extra backup rotation for the first 2 weeks (estimated 3 hours/week of on-call overhead); legal tells me we can offer a limited credit if they need it but recommend no credits if scope is enforced.

Recommendation: approve the temporary amendment with the compensating controls above, require a daily Slack status in #finnovate-ops for first week and a post-mortem if any P1 is triggered.

If you approve I will: 1) finalize the amendment, 2) loop in Legal for sign-off, 3) schedule the runbook update and on-call burn-in.

Ben
Sr. Ops Eng (On-call)
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Sep 8, 2025 at 4:03 PM Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben — forwarding an ask from a mid-market customer (Finnovate)...

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@finnovate.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Night maintenance overlap — ask for temporary P2 response window

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear context and for sharing the schedule. Apologies for the slightly slow turnaround; we wanted to align on controls before confirming.

We can approve a temporary, scoped amendment with the following terms:
- Scope: payment-batch cluster only (by service tag).
- Effective window: 2025-09-12 00:00 PT through 2025-10-02 23:59 PT.
- P1 SLA: unchanged (1 hour initial response).
- P2 SLA (00:00–06:00 PT only): initial response target extended to 4 hours. Outside that window, standard P2 targets remain in effect.
- Compensating controls: automated end-to-end failure detectors for batch jobs (will promote to P1), nightly health-checks, and a daily status post in our shared Slack channel for the first week.
- Escalation path: primary on-call -> payments secondary -> engineering lead. If any actual degradation impacting settlement occurs we will immediately promote to P1.

Next steps:
1) Ben will finalize the amendment text and share an editable draft.
2) We will route the amendment to Legal for a short-form sign-off; once signed we'll push a DocuSign link.
3) We'll update the payment-batch runbook and do a one-night burn-in before 2025-09-12.

If that all looks good, Ben will circulate the amendment and I will send the formal DocuSign.

Michael Grant
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: signed-amendment-stub.pdf (will be replaced by DocuSign final when completed)
